B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: IFTTT states MCP is available on all IFTTT plans. Tool capabilities are plan-gated: Free can search and create or enable free Applets within quota; Pro adds actions and Pro Applets; Pro+ adds queries and Pro+ Applets. No separate MCP fee is stated.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: IFTTT Free: $0; Pro: $2.99/month when billed annually ($35.88/year); Pro+: $8.99/month when billed annually ($107.88/year).
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page lists Free with 2 Applets, Pro with 20 Applets, and Pro+ with unlimited Applets. It also lists tier-dependent features including faster runs, multiple actions, exclusive triggers/actions, queries and filters, and multiple accounts per service.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: The IFTTT account must authorize the MCP connection and services must be connected individually. The client also needs to support remote MCP and OAuth. Some clients require paid plans or developer/beta settings. Product tier limits which MCP operations and Applets are available.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: IFTTT controls product-plan entitlements and service availability; the user controls account authorization and connected services; the MCP client controls client-side enablement and its own access requirements.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The published tool overview distinguishes discovery/read tools from Applet lifecycle and direct execution tools. Client materials identify `run_action` as real-world side-effecting and `remove_applet` as permanent. MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) are NOT FOUND; hosted schemas were unavailable. 2. Server-enforced confirmation is NOT FOUND. Bundled client rules recommend confirmation before `create_applet`, `remove_applet`, and side-effecting `run_action`; these are client-side recommendations, not evidence of server enforcement. 3. OAuth uses the single scope `mcp`; product plan gates features; the setup skill says services require separate connections and describes connect/reconnect URLs. Inheritance of account roles, admin switches, allowlists, redirect-URI approval policy, and token lifetime are NOT FOUND. A revocation endpoint is published. 4. No read-only endpoint, toolset filter, query-free switch, or region-specific endpoint was found. Plans restrict which operations are available. 5. Privacy policy applies to IFTTT service data generally; MCP-specific masking, PII exclusion, or field-level boundaries are NOT FOUND. Service connections are account-specific. 6. Plans list Applet quotas (Free 2, Pro 20, Pro+ unlimited); the client skill notes an Applet action delay up to 14,145 seconds. MCP rate limits, result truncation, and per-call costs are NOT FOUND. 7. Client materials describe structured validation errors and say to fix named fields; schemas and server coercion, unknown-argument rejection, or parameter overrides are NOT FOUND. 8. MCP-specific audit trails, telemetry, and opt-out are NOT FOUND in reviewed sources. 9. The official 20-name list contains no feedback, rating, report, or survey tool. No tool-result upsell was documented; official pages include promotional trial/plan language. 10. Bundled Cursor rules and setup/build skills deliver behavioral guidance outside the MCP server. They advise discovery instead of guessing identifiers, confirmations, template reuse, and waiting for service connection. 11. Whether previous agent behavior changes later output or available tools/resources is NOT FOUND. 12. A flat published list of 20 names is documented; the server dispatches actions and queries across IFTTT services according to client documentation. Evidence does not establish nested MCP subservers. 13. No arbitrary API request, SQL, script execution, or raw-code tool appears in the official tool list. Filter Code is described as natural-language input processed server-side, not raw TypeScript/JavaScript.

[LOCAL CODE @85869bb, bundled client rule] “`create_applet` enables the Applet immediately. Summarize what the Applet will do (trigger, actions, and any queries or delay) and get the user's confirmation before creating it.”

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: Official evidence describes one hosted endpoint with one published tool list. Tools dispatch IFTTT operations across connected services, but evidence does not show hierarchical MCP servers or dynamically selected toolsets.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The MCP tool overview does not include account billing or plan management, although IFTTT exposes Free, Pro, and Pro+ plans. It also does not list developer platform/API publishing tools, which the pricing page describes as a Pro+ developer feature. These are absent from the published MCP overview; this evidence does not establish that every such operation is unavailable through all other IFTTT interfaces.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The bundled plugin rules recommend confirmation before creating an immediately enabled Applet and before permanent removal or real-world actions; they also direct agents to discover identifiers, copy step templates, and wait for service connection before retrying. These are client-side files, not documented server-enforced controls. The product page encourages describing goals in natural language and says the assistant can act across connected services.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The linked privacy policy says IFTTT takes the private nature of personal information seriously and describes how it uses and protects information collected through its site and services. The reviewed policy and MCP pages do not specify MCP-specific prompt handling, AI training use, retention period, or MCP audit controls.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: IFTTT says the MCP connection gives assistants access to connected services and can search, build, and run automations. Its documentation says MCP is available on all IFTTT plans, with capabilities depending on tier. It describes service authentication and maintenance as handled by IFTTT.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The public OAuth metadata verifies authentication and a single `mcp` scope. Product documentation and client files describe tier gates, service connections, and confirmation recommendations. The confirmation recommendations are not shown to be enforced by server code. Privacy and data-protection claims are general policy statements; MCP-specific handling and logging could not be checked against the closed hosted implementation.

contradictions: The official repository's tool overview names 20 tools, while Anthropic's Claude connector directory and other catalogues list 14. The 14 listed by Anthropic are a subset; the official client repository additionally names get_steps, my_applets, edit_applet, disable_applet, remove_applet, and set_applet_filter_code.

The OAuth metadata exposes only the single scope `mcp`, while official product documentation describes different plan-based access to searching, Applet creation/enabling, actions, and queries. The reviewed sources do not clarify whether plan gates are enforced independently of OAuth scope.
observations_for_research: The official client distribution packages behavioral rules and skills separately from the hosted MCP endpoint; their presence in a client may vary.
A fixed 20-name tool interface exposes operations over a large catalogue of connected IFTTT services, while the OAuth metadata publishes only one MCP scope.
